## 2026-08-04 | ERCOT BESS Fleet (32 Nodes)

---

## 1. PERFORMANCE SUMMARY

Yesterday's fleet average RT settled at **$23.65/MWh**, marking a notable **cooldown from the $29–$37/MWh range** observed over the prior three days (July 31–August 2), where spike node counts ran 6–12 per day. Yesterday's spike activity was concentrated at just **three nodes** — OLNEYTN_RN, MAINLAND_RN, and RUSSEKST_RN — with OLNEYTN_RN reaching a fleet peak of **$1,507.78/MWh**, likely driven by the binding 6830__B constraint (CRDSW→OLNEY) which averaged a $181.28/MWh shadow price with a peak of $820.78/MWh at HE18. POTEETS_RN traded into **negative territory**, creating a charging opportunity for assets positioned there. On the DART dimension, MAINLAND_RN posted the largest RT outperformance with RT exceeding DA by **$14.33/MWh** — assets dispatching in RT at that node captured materially higher prices than the DA commitment would have delivered. Conversely, JUNCTION_RN and POTEETS_RN posted DA premiums of **$10.98 and $10.76/MWh**, respectively, rewarding DA-committed assets at those locations. The aggregate picture is a fleet bifurcating cleanly between high-volatility congestion-driven nodes (North Texas corridor, South Texas) and stable DA-premium nodes (West/Central Texas), with no fleet-wide stress event but meaningful locational dispersion.

---

## 2. DISPATCH STRATEGY BY NODE

Nodes with **negative MCC exposure** in this group (TYNAN_RN: -$148.48/MWh, WLTC_ESR_RN: -$146.97/MWh, FALFUR_RN: -$150.65/MWh, POTEETS_RN: -$146.50/MWh) are absorbing meaningful congestion costs — DA commitment locks in the premium and avoids incremental RT congestion exposure at these locations.

## 3. CONSTRAINT ANALYSIS

### 🔴 610__B (TMPSW → TMPSE) — CRITICAL
**Avg shadow $1,130.11/MWh | Peak $1,867.89/MWh | 3 hours binding | Peak HE18**
This is the highest-severity constraint in the fleet by average shadow price. Exposed HEN nodes: **JDKNS_RN, SADLBACK_RN, CEDRVALE_RN, TOYAH_RN**. At an average shadow of $1,130/MWh, even a modest positive shift factor at these nodes would translate to a commercially significant MCC. JDKNS_RN's MCC of +$13.70/MWh and the others in the +$11–$12/MWh range confirm **positive SF × positive shadow = congestion benefit** — these nodes are located on the unconstrained (load) side of this constraint. The 3-hour binding window peaked at HE18, consistent with peak AC load and solar ramp-down. **Flag as commercially significant** — DA commitment at these nodes captures this congestion premium reliably.

### 🔴 1715__B (TMPSW → FRYSW) — HIGH SEVERITY
**Avg shadow $338.71/MWh | Peak $969.81/MWh | 8 hours binding | Peak HE14**
Same node exposure as 610__B (JDKNS_RN, SADLBACK_RN, CEDRVALE_RN, TOYAH_RN). With 8 hours of binding duration and a peak at HE14, this constraint spans the full afternoon peak window and aligns with maximum solar output — the constraint likely reflects transmission limits on the West Texas export corridor during high solar generation periods. MCC benefits confirmed at these four nodes (~$12–$14/MWh range). **Combined with 610__B exposure, these nodes are sitting at a congestion sweet spot — high-confidence DA commitment.**

### 🟠 6830__B (CRDSW → OLNEY) — NORTH TEXAS
**Avg shadow $181.28/MWh | Peak $820.78/MWh | 7 hours binding | Peak HE18**
Exposed HEN nodes: **CISC_RN, MNWL_BESS_RN, OLNEYTN_RN**. OLNEYTN_RN's MCC of +$246.54/MWh is the **highest positive MCC in the entire fleet** — this node is clearly on the benefit side of this North Texas constraint. CISC_RN (+$91.18) and MNWL_BESS_RN (+$141.09) also capture material congestion benefits. The 7-hour binding duration and HE18 peak align with Wichita Falls temperatures of 106°F today — afternoon load stress is expected to persist. **All three nodes are high-conviction positions; OLNEYTN_RN's RT spike risk is real but the MCC benefit is structural.**

**Avg shadow $179.00/MWh | Peak $251.41/MWh | 5 hours binding | Peak HE19**

HOLCOMB_RN1's MCC of **-$137.91/MWh** signals a **negative SF** — this node is on the constrained (generation) side, meaning the binding constraint is a net cost. CATARINA_B1 at -$95.11/MWh and HAMI_BESS_RN at -$76.34/MWh similarly reflect congestion costs. **These nodes are commercially disadvantaged in RT during binding hours (HE15–HE19) — DA commitment is specifically recommended to lock in DA prices before RT congestion erodes value.**

**Avg shadow $54.55/MWh | Peak $88.83/MWh | 5 hours binding | Peak HE11**
Exposed HEN nodes: **CATARINA_B1, HOLCOMB_RN1, RUSSEKST_RN, TOYAH_RN**. The MCC impact is secondary to PALOUS_WOLFCA1_1 for the same nodes but compounds the congestion cost burden at CATARINA_B1 and HOLCOMB_RN1. Monitor for concurrent binding with PALOUS during the 10AM–7PM window.

## 4. WEATHER & LOAD OUTLOOK

Today's conditions are **intensely bullish for ERCOT afternoon peak pricing**, with Wichita Falls at **106°F** (OLNEYTN_RN corridor), Dallas-Fort Worth at **102°F**, Abilene at **102°F**, and Laredo at **102°F** — a broad heat dome covering most of the ERCOT footprint. This heat persistence, combined with gross load already at **86.9 GW** yesterday, suggests today's load will challenge or exceed that level — watch for ERCOT emergency alerts if wind underperforms (24.6 GW yesterday). The ECRS_DAM contribution of $2,800/MW/yr to HEN vs. zero in the baseline highlights the ancillary service differentiation — this aligns with the forward AS strategy to continue prioritizing NSPIN and ECRS DA offers in peak hours.
